body:
We're getting reports of similar crashes in our released android games reported to us via sentry.io. We started getting these reports after upgrading from Godot 3.5 to 4.3

I couldn't reproduce using the adb command to change uimode night, but it does reproduce by the user changing font size in android settings.

You can also change font size with adb and reproduce the crash:
adb shell settings put system font_scale 1.0
adb shell settings put system font_scale 1.1

The crash reproduces in the Godot 4.3 editor in the google play store.  But it does not reproduce in Godot 3.6 editor

Android is destroying and recreating the GodotApp activity, which Godot doesn't handle well at all. 

A work around for this crash is to add all the config options to android:configChanges  in AndroidManifest.xml:
android:configChanges="orientation|keyboardHidden|screenSize|smallestScreenSize|density|keyboard|navigation|screenLayout|uiMode|fontScale|fontWeightAdjustment|colorMode|grammaticalGender|layoutDirection|locale|mcc|mnc|touchscreen"

But I don't know if other things can also trigger android to destroy and recreate the activity without restarting the app. So hopefully the crash can be fixed too.

We released an update last week with everything added to android:configChanges like above, but still got reports of similar crashes:

```
Exception Type: Unknown (SIGABRT)

Application Specific Information:
Abort

Thread 0 Crashed:
0   libc.so                         0x7dd14fda44        abort
1   libc.so                         0x7dd14ff8bc        <unknown> + 540382591164
2   libc.so                         0x7dd156d9ac        <unknown> + 540383041964
3   libc.so                         0x7dd156d830        pthread_mutex_lock
4   split_config.arm64_v8a.apk      0x7cacd60d30        [inlined] std::__ndk1::__libcpp_recursive_mutex_lock (__threading_support:347)
5   split_config.arm64_v8a.apk      0x7cacd60d30        std::__ndk1::recursive_mutex::lock (mutex.cpp:71)
6   split_config.arm64_v8a.apk      0x7cab408950        [inlined] std::__ndk1::unique_lock<T>::unique_lock (__mutex_base:119)
7   split_config.arm64_v8a.apk      0x7cab408950        [inlined] MutexLock<T>::MutexLock (mutex.h:81)
8   split_config.arm64_v8a.apk      0x7cab408950        ResourceUID::load_from_cache (resource_uid.cpp:178)
9   split_config.arm64_v8a.apk      0x7ca904fa68        Main::setup (main.cpp:1824)
10  split_config.arm64_v8a.apk      0x7ca9031c1c        Java_org_godotengine_godot_GodotLib_setup (java_godot_lib_jni.cpp:190)
11  base.odex                       0x7cde2d185c        <unknown> + 536303442012
```

I'm pretty certain it is the same problem where android is destroying and recreating the activity without restarting the app because sentry also reports these events right before the crash:
```
Ui Lifecycle info 04:53:43.018 AM
{
data: {"screen":"GodotApp","state":"destroyed"}
}

Ui Lifecycle info 04:53:45.328 AM
{
data: {"screen":"GodotApp","state":"created"}
}
```

But I don't know what exactly is triggering the activity restart.

I'm trying to find a solution for this. Maybe it's enough if we delay the start and wait until the GodotEngine has completely shut down.

https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/resources/runtime-changes

> Some configuration changes always cause the activity to restart. You can't disable them. For example, you can't disable the [dynamic colors change](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/theming/dynamic-colors) introduced in Android 12L (API level 32).

From https://www.reddit.com/r/androiddev/s/rqkYL8aSNF, we may be able to distinguish when the activity is being recreated using https://developer.android.com/reference/android/app/Activity#isChangingConfigurations()
@Alex2782 Let me take a look at resolving this issue. I believe there may be an approach by leveraging the `GodotService` class being implemented in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102866

I was wondering if this is still an issue in Godot 4.5.1 and tested using Godot 4.5.1 from Google Play Store running on Android 16 on a Pixel 9

Changing nightmode like in the original post does not reproduce.

Changing font_scale with adb like in my reply above does still cause Godot to exit, not sure if it's really a crash though, here's the logcat:

[logcat.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23556998/logcat.txt)


Changing Wallpaper color also causes Godot to exit with a different logcat:

1. Install and run Godot 4.5.1 from Google Play
2. Goto Android Settings -> Wallpaper & Style
3. Swipe over to Home Screen,  scroll down tap on Colors
4. Change color,  tap Apply and back out of settings
5. Godot immediately exits with the following logcat:

[wallpaper-logcat.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23557022/wallpaper-logcat.txt)


My main concern with this issue was to fix crashes being reported to Google Play Console.  I'm not sure if either of these qualifies as a crash since it looks like godot is shutting down normally.    So maybe it's ok now?
